subject: B
topic: All topics of GK & Current Affairs India (mixed)

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Polavaram Project', a major multipurpose irrigation project, is being constructed on which river?
questions.explanation: The Polavaram Project is on the Godavari river in Andhra Pradesh. 'Krishna' is wrong — it has projects like Nagarjuna Sagar. 'Cauvery' is wrong — it flows through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. 'Mahanadi' is wrong — it has Hirakud Dam in Odisha.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC):

(i) It is a statutory body established under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.
(ii) The chairperson is a retired Chief Justice of India.
(iii) It can investigate violations of human rights by the armed forces.
(iv) It has the power to award compensation to victims directly.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: NHRC is statutory under the PHRA 1993 (i correct). Chairperson is a retired CJI (ii correct). (iii) is wrong because NHRC cannot directly investigate armed forces complaints — it can only seek reports from the government. (iv) is wrong because NHRC can only recommend compensation; it cannot directly award it. Option 2 includes (iii). Option 3 includes both (iii) and (iv). Option 4 excludes (i).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India has a federal system with a unitary bias.
Reason (R): The Indian Constitution provides for a strong Centre with residuary powers, single citizenship, and the ability to alter state boundaries without state consent.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: India is federal with unitary tilt (A correct). R lists specific unitary features — residuary powers with Centre, single citizenship, power to alter state boundaries (R correct and explains the 'unitary bias'). Option 2 is wrong because R directly demonstrates the unitary bias. Option 3 is wrong because R is correct. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following national parks with the states they are located in:

Column I:
(a) Sundarbans National Park
(b) Bandipur National Park
(c) Gir National Park
(d) Kanha National Park

Column II:
(i) Gujarat
(ii) Karnataka
(iii) West Bengal
(iv) Madhya Pradesh

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Sundarbans is in West Bengal (iii), famous for Royal Bengal Tigers. Bandipur is in Karnataka (ii). Gir is in Gujarat (i), home of Asiatic Lions. Kanha is in Madhya Pradesh (iv). Option 2 swaps Sundarbans and Bandipur. Option 3 swaps Bandipur and Kanha. Option 4 swaps Sundarbans and Gir.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are objectives of the World Trade Organization (WTO)?

(i) To promote free and fair trade among member nations
(ii) To settle trade disputes between countries
(iii) To provide military assistance to developing nations
(iv) To reduce tariffs and other barriers to trade

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: WTO promotes free trade (i correct), settles disputes (ii correct), and reduces trade barriers (iv correct). (iii) is wrong because WTO deals exclusively with trade — military assistance is the domain of defence alliances, not WTO. Option 2 includes (iii). Option 3 excludes (ii). Option 4 includes (iii).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The concept of 'Judicial Review' in India means:
options: The power of courts to examine the constitutionality of laws
The review of lower court judgments by higher courts
The process of appointing new judges
questions.correctAnswer: The power of courts to examine the constitutionality of laws
questions.explanation: Judicial Review empowers courts (especially SC and HCs) to declare laws unconstitutional if they violate the Constitution. 'Review of lower court judgments' is wrong — that's the appellate jurisdiction. 'Performance review of judges' is wrong — that's not a constitutional concept. 'Appointing judges' is wrong — that's the collegium/appointment process.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about India's nuclear power programme:

(i) India's first nuclear reactor was 'Apsara', commissioned in 1956.
(ii) The Department of Atomic Energy is headed by the Prime Minister.
(iii) Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant in Tamil Nadu uses pressurized water reactors.
(iv) India is a signatory to the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty (CTBT).

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Apsara was India's first research reactor (1956) (i correct). Kudankulam uses Russian VVER (PWR) technology (iii correct). (ii) is wrong — DAE is directly under the PM's office but headed by a Secretary/Chairman of AEC, not the PM personally. (iv) is wrong — India has NOT signed the CTBT. Option 2 includes (ii). Option 3 includes (iv). Option 4 includes both.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act' was passed by the Indian Parliament in:
questions.explanation: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act was passed in 2013 after the anti-corruption movement. '2011' is wrong — that year saw the Anna Hazare movement but the Act wasn't passed yet. '2015' is wrong — too late. '2010' is wrong — the demand was building but no legislation then.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Monsoon season in India typically lasts from June to September.
Reason (R): The Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) shifts northward during summer, pulling moisture-laden winds from the Indian Ocean towards the Indian subcontinent.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: SW monsoon is June-September (A correct). The ITCZ shift pulls moisture from the Indian Ocean (R correct and explains the monsoon mechanism). Option 2 is wrong because R explains the atmospheric physics behind the monsoon. Option 3 is wrong because R is correct. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following Indian states with their folk dances:

Column I:
(a) Punjab
(b) Gujarat
(c) Assam
(d) Rajasthan

Column II:
(i) Ghoomar
(ii) Bhangra
(iii) Bihu
(iv) Garba

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Punjab = Bhangra (ii). Gujarat = Garba (iv). Assam = Bihu (iii). Rajasthan = Ghoomar (i). Option 2 swaps Punjab and Gujarat. Option 3 swaps Gujarat and Assam. Option 4 swaps Punjab and Rajasthan.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Namami Gange Programme' is primarily related to:
options: Cleaning and rejuvenation of the river Ganga
Construction of dams for flood control
questions.correctAnswer: Cleaning and rejuvenation of the river Ganga
questions.explanation: Namami Gange (launched 2014) aims at effective abatement of pollution, conservation, and rejuvenation of the Ganga. 'Promoting inland waterways' is wrong — that's Sagarmala/Jal Marg Vikas. 'Dam construction' is wrong — separate projects. 'Fish cultivation' is wrong — that's Blue Revolution.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Inter-State Council:

(i) It is a constitutional body established under Article 263.
(ii) It is chaired by the Prime Minister.
(iii) It promotes coordination between the Centre and States.
(iv) Its recommendations are binding on both Centre and States.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: ISC is under Art. 263 (i correct). Chaired by PM (ii correct). Promotes Centre-State coordination (iii correct). (iv) is wrong because ISC's recommendations are advisory/deliberative — not legally binding. Option 2 includes (iv). Option 3 excludes (ii). Option 4 includes (iv).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Indian Constitution provides for an independent judiciary.
Reason (R): Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts are appointed through a transparent process and can only be removed by a special majority of Parliament through an address.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: India has an independent judiciary (A correct). Security of tenure and difficult removal process ensures independence (R correct and explains how independence is guaranteed). Option 2 is wrong because R describes the mechanism of independence. Option 3 is wrong because R is correct. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Asiatic Society' was founded in Calcutta in 1784 by:
questions.explanation: Sir William Jones founded the Asiatic Society in 1784 to study Oriental cultures. 'Warren Hastings' is wrong — he was Governor-General who patronized it but didn't found it. 'Lord Wellesley' is wrong — he came later (1798). 'Lord Cornwallis' is wrong — he was GG from 1786.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The 'Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana' (PMGSY) aims to provide all-weather road connectivity to __________ habitations.
questions.explanation: PMGSY connects unconnected rural habitations with populations over 500 (250 in hilly/tribal areas) via all-weather roads. 'Urban slum' is wrong — PMGSY is rural-focused. 'Hilly border' is wrong — too specific. 'Coastal fishing' is wrong — not the scheme's target.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are Fundamental Rights that are available to both citizens and non-citizens (foreigners) in India?

(i) Right to Equality (Article 14)
(ii) Right to Freedom of Speech (Article 19)
(iii) Right to Life and Personal Liberty (Article 21)
(iv) Right against Exploitation (Article 23-24)

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Art. 14 (Equality) applies to all persons (i correct). Art. 21 (Life/Liberty) applies to all persons (iii correct). Art. 23-24 (Against Exploitation) applies to all (iv correct). Art. 19 (ii) is wrong because freedoms under Article 19 are available ONLY to citizens, not foreigners. Option 2 includes (ii). Option 3 excludes (iv). Option 4 includes (ii).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Deccan Plateau' is bounded on the west by the:
questions.explanation: The Western Ghats form the western boundary of the Deccan Plateau, running parallel to the western coast. 'Eastern Ghats' is wrong — they bound it on the east. 'Vindhya Range' is wrong — it's on the northern boundary. 'Aravalli Hills' is wrong — they're in Rajasthan, northwest of the Deccan.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India follows the system of 'Universal Adult Suffrage'.
Reason (R): Every Indian citizen who has completed 18 years of age has the right to vote, regardless of caste, religion, gender, or economic status.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: India has Universal Adult Suffrage (A correct). R defines what this means — voting for all 18+ citizens without discrimination (R correct and is the very definition of A). Option 2 is wrong because R defines the concept in A. Option 3 is wrong because R is correct. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'National Green Tribunal' (NGT) was established under which Act?
questions.explanation: NGT was established by the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 for effective and expeditious disposal of environmental cases. 'Environment Protection Act, 1986' is wrong — that's the umbrella environmental law. 'Forest Conservation Act, 1980' is wrong — deals with forest diversion. 'Wildlife Protection Act, 1972' is wrong — protects wildlife.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following rivers with the states where they drain into the sea:

Column I:
(a) Ganga
(b) Narmada
(c) Krishna
(d) Brahmaputra

Column II:
(i) Andhra Pradesh
(ii) Gujarat
(iii) West Bengal/Bangladesh
(iv) Assam/Bangladesh

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Ganga enters the sea via West Bengal/Bangladesh (iii). Narmada drains into Gulf of Khambhat, Gujarat (ii). Krishna enters the Bay of Bengal in Andhra Pradesh (i). Brahmaputra flows through Assam into Bangladesh (iv). Option 2 swaps Ganga and Narmada. Option 3 swaps Narmada and Krishna. Option 4 swaps Ganga and Brahmaputra.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The concept of 'Concurrent List' in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from:
questions.explanation: The Concurrent List (subjects on which both Centre and States can legislate) was borrowed from the Australian Constitution. 'Canada' is wrong — India took federal structure with strong Centre from Canada. 'Ireland' is wrong — DPSPs came from Ireland. 'South Africa' is wrong — procedure of constitutional amendment came from there.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Niti Aayog:

(i) It is headed by the Prime Minister as its chairperson.
(ii) It replaced the Planning Commission in 2015.
(iii) It has the power to allocate funds to states.
(iv) It functions as a think tank for the government.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: PM chairs NITI Aayog (i correct). Replaced Planning Commission Jan 2015 (ii correct). Functions as a think tank (iv correct). (iii) is wrong because NITI Aayog does NOT allocate funds — that power rests with the Finance Commission and the Finance Ministry. Option 2 includes (iii). Option 3 excludes (ii). Option 4 includes (iii).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Param Vir Chakra' is India's highest military decoration. It is awarded for:
options: Most conspicuous bravery or self-sacrifice in the presence of the enemy
Distinguished service of a high order to the nation
Long and meritorious service in the armed forces
questions.correctAnswer: Most conspicuous bravery or self-sacrifice in the presence of the enemy
questions.explanation: PVC is for the most conspicuous bravery/self-sacrifice facing the enemy. 'Distinguished service' is wrong — that's Padma awards domain. 'Military science' is wrong — not PVC's criterion. 'Long service' is wrong — that's service medals, not gallantry awards.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The Constitution of India was adopted on __________ and came into effect on __________.
questions.explanation: Constitution adopted on 26 Nov 1949, effective 26 Jan 1950 (Republic Day). '26 Jan 1950; 15 Aug 1950' is wrong — reverses and adds wrong date. '15 Aug 1947; 26 Jan 1950' is wrong — 15 Aug 1947 was Independence Day, not adoption. '26 Nov 1949; 15 Aug 1950' is wrong — wrong effective date.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India is the largest democracy in the world.
Reason (R): India has the largest number of eligible voters and conducts regular free and fair elections at multiple levels of government.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: India is the world's largest democracy (A correct). Having the most voters and regular multi-level elections makes it the largest functioning democracy (R correct and explains why India holds this title). Option 2 is wrong because R explains what makes India the largest democracy. Option 3 is wrong because R is correct. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following pairs of international organizations and their headquarters are correctly matched?

(i) WHO — Geneva
(ii) WTO — New York
(iii) IMF — Washington D.C.
(iv) UNICEF — New York

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: WHO is in Geneva (i correct). IMF is in Washington D.C. (iii correct). UNICEF HQ is in New York (iv correct). (ii) is wrong because WTO headquarters is in Geneva, Switzerland, NOT New York. Option 2 includes (ii). Option 3 excludes (iv). Option 4 includes (ii).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Indira Awas Yojana' (now Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin) is primarily aimed at:
options: Providing housing to rural BPL families
questions.correctAnswer: Providing housing to rural BPL families
questions.explanation: IAY/PMAY-G provides pucca houses to rural BPL/homeless families. 'Urban housing for middle-income' is wrong — that's PMAY-Urban. 'Industrial worker accommodation' is wrong — not the scheme's target. 'Student hostels' is wrong — unrelated scheme.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Space Programme:

(i) PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle) is primarily used for launching satellites into Sun-Synchronous Polar Orbits.
(ii) GSLV (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle) uses cryogenic engines for upper stage.
(iii) India's Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) was launched in 2013.
(iv) ISRO's headquarters is in Thiruvananthapuram.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: PSLV launches into polar/sun-synchronous orbits (i correct). GSLV uses cryogenic upper stage (ii correct). Mangalyaan launched Nov 2013 (iii correct). (iv) is wrong because ISRO HQ is in Bengaluru, not Thiruvananthapuram (which houses Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre). Option 2 includes (iv). Option 3 excludes (ii). Option 4 includes (iv).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Regulating Act of 1773' is significant in Indian history because:
options: It was the first step by the British Parliament to regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India
It established the Indian National Congress
It abolished the Dual Government in Bengal
questions.correctAnswer: It was the first step by the British Parliament to regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India
questions.explanation: The Regulating Act 1773 was the first act of British Parliament to control EIC's territorial acquisitions in India. 'Granted independence' is wrong — that was 1947. 'Established INC' is wrong — INC was founded in 1885. 'Abolished Dual Government' is wrong — that was abolished earlier by Robert Clive's reforms.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following tribes with the states they are primarily associated with:

Column I:
(a) Bhil
(b) Santhal
(c) Naga
(d) Toda

Column II:
(i) Tamil Nadu (Nilgiris)
(ii) Rajasthan/Gujarat
(iii) Nagaland
(iv) Jharkhand

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Bhil tribe is in Rajasthan/Gujarat (ii). Santhal in Jharkhand (iv). Naga in Nagaland (iii). Toda in Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu (i). Option 2 swaps Bhil and Santhal. Option 3 swaps Santhal and Naga. Option 4 swaps Bhil and Toda.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Bharat Stage VI' (BS-VI) emission norms were implemented in India from:
questions.explanation: India leapfrogged from BS-IV to BS-VI norms on 1 April 2020. '1 April 2018' is wrong — BS-IV was still in place then. '1 April 2022' is wrong — too late. '1 January 2020' is wrong — the switch was from 1 April, not January.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the 'Right to Education' (RTE) Act, 2009:

(i) It provides free and compulsory education to children aged 6-14 years.
(ii) It mandates a 25% reservation for economically weaker sections in private schools.
(iii) It was enacted under Article 21A of the Constitution.
(iv) It applies uniformly to all states including J&K from its inception.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: RTE covers ages 6-14 (i correct). 25% EWS reservation in private schools (ii correct). Under Art. 21A (iii correct). (iv) is wrong because RTE did NOT apply to J&K initially due to Article 370 — it was extended after abrogation in 2019. Option 2 includes (iv). Option 3 excludes (ii). Option 4 includes (iv).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows India's installed power capacity (in GW) by source as of 2024:

| Source | Capacity (GW) |
|---|---|
| Thermal (Coal+Gas) | 240 |
| Renewable (Solar+Wind+Others) | 180 |
| Hydro | 47 |
| Nuclear | 8 |

What is the approximate percentage share of Renewable energy in total installed capacity?
questions.explanation: Total = 240+180+47+8 = 475 GW. Renewable % = (180/475)×100 ≈ 37.9%. '45%' is wrong — overestimates. '30%' is wrong — underestimates. '25%' is wrong — far too low.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Partition of Bengal' in 1905 was carried out by:
questions.explanation: Lord Curzon, Viceroy (1899-1905), partitioned Bengal in 1905 to weaken the nationalist movement. 'Lord Dalhousie' is wrong — he left India in 1856. 'Lord Mountbatten' is wrong — he was the last Viceroy (1947). 'Lord Ripon' is wrong — he was Viceroy 1880-1884.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are features of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India?

(i) It is a destination-based consumption tax.
(ii) It subsumes multiple indirect taxes into one.
(iii) The GST Council decides tax rates by majority voting.
(iv) Alcohol for human consumption is included under GST.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: GST is destination-based (i correct). It subsumed multiple taxes (ii correct). (iii) is wrong — GST Council decisions are taken by 3/4th majority with weighted voting (Centre 1/3, States 2/3), not simple majority. (iv) is wrong — alcohol for human consumption is EXCLUDED from GST. Option 2 includes (iii). Option 3 includes both (iii) and (iv). Option 4 includes both.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Himalayas are young fold mountains.
Reason (R): They were formed by the collision of the Indian tectonic plate with the Eurasian plate during the Cenozoic era, and are still rising.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Himalayas are young fold mountains (A correct). They formed from India-Eurasia plate collision in Cenozoic era and are still rising (R correct and explains both their origin and 'young' classification). Option 2 is wrong because R directly explains how they formed. Option 3 is wrong because R is geologically correct. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Swamitva Scheme' launched in 2020 aims to:
options: Provide property cards to rural household owners using drone technology
Distribute free land to landless farmers
Map urban properties for tax collection
questions.correctAnswer: Provide property cards to rural household owners using drone technology
questions.explanation: SVAMITVA uses drones to map rural residential land and issue property cards/ownership records. 'Distribute free land' is wrong — it's about documentation, not redistribution. 'Survey forest land' is wrong — different from residential mapping. 'Map urban properties' is wrong — it targets RURAL areas.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Indian judiciary:

(i) The Supreme Court has original, appellate, and advisory jurisdictions.
(ii) Article 32 empowers the Supreme Court to issue writs for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
(iii) The Supreme Court can transfer cases from one High Court to another.
(iv) All judges of the Supreme Court must have practiced law for at least 20 years.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: SC has original, appellate, advisory jurisdictions (i correct). Art. 32 for writs (ii correct). SC can transfer cases between HCs under Art. 139A (iii correct). (iv) is wrong — the requirement is 10 years as HC advocate or 5 years as HC judge, or being a distinguished jurist — NOT 20 years. Option 2 includes (iv). Option 3 excludes (iii). Option 4 includes (iv).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows voter turnout in recent Indian General Elections:

| Election Year | Turnout (%) |
|---|---|
| 2009 | 58.2 |
| 2014 | 66.4 |
| 2019 | 67.4 |
| 2024 | 65.8 |

In which election year was the highest voter turnout recorded?
questions.explanation: 2019 had the highest turnout at 67.4%. '2024' is wrong — 65.8% is lower. '2014' is wrong — 66.4% is second highest. '2009' is wrong — 58.2% is the lowest listed.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Ilbert Bill' controversy of 1883 was related to:
options: The right of Indian judges to try European offenders
The freedom of the Indian press
questions.correctAnswer: The right of Indian judges to try European offenders
questions.explanation: The Ilbert Bill proposed allowing Indian judges/magistrates to try European British subjects — causing huge controversy among Europeans. 'Freedom of press' is wrong — that was Vernacular Press Act. 'Partition of Bengal' is wrong — that was 1905. 'Indian railways' is wrong — unrelated.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following constitutional amendments with their provisions:

Column I:
(a) 42nd Amendment
(b) 44th Amendment
(c) 61st Amendment
(d) 86th Amendment

Column II:
(i) Lowered voting age from 21 to 18
(ii) Added 'Socialist, Secular, Integrity' to Preamble
(iii) Added Right to Education (Article 21A)
(iv) Restored Right to Property as a legal right, not fundamental

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: 42nd Amendment (1976) added Socialist/Secular/Integrity (ii). 44th Amendment (1978) made Right to Property a legal right only (iv). 61st Amendment (1988) lowered voting age (i). 86th Amendment (2002) added Art. 21A for education (iii). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (a) and (c).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Chipko Movement' is primarily associated with:
questions.explanation: Chipko Movement (1970s, Uttarakhand) was about hugging trees to prevent deforestation. 'Water harvesting' is wrong — different environmental cause. 'Wildlife protection' is wrong — that's Project Tiger/Elephant. 'Air pollution' is wrong — unrelated.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Finance Commission:

(i) It is a constitutional body under Article 280.
(ii) It is constituted every 5 years.
(iii) It recommends the distribution of tax revenue between Centre and States.
(iv) Its recommendations are binding on the government.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: FC is constitutional under Art. 280 (i correct). Constituted every 5 years (ii correct). Recommends tax revenue distribution (iii correct). (iv) is wrong because FC recommendations are advisory — the government generally accepts them but is not legally bound. Option 2 includes (iv). Option 3 excludes (ii). Option 4 includes (iv).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows India's foreign exchange reserves (in USD billion) over 4 years:

| Year | Reserves (USD bn) |
|---|---|
| 2021 | 577 |
| 2022 | 532 |
| 2023 | 617 |
| 2024 | 656 |

What was the increase in reserves from 2022 to 2024?
questions.explanation: Increase = 656 – 532 = $124 billion. '$85 billion' is wrong — that's 617–532. '$79 billion' is wrong — that's 656–577. '$139 billion' is wrong — overcalculation.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The term 'Bicameralism' in Indian governance refers to:
options: A legislature with two houses (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha)
The system of two levels of judiciary
questions.correctAnswer: A legislature with two houses (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha)
questions.explanation: Bicameralism means a two-chambered legislature — Lok Sabha (Lower) and Rajya Sabha (Upper). 'Two-party system' is wrong — India has multi-party, not two-party. 'Two levels of judiciary' is wrong — India has three levels. 'Dual citizenship' is wrong — India has single citizenship.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following correctly describes the 'Right to Constitutional Remedies' (Article 32)?

(i) It is called the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution by Dr. Ambedkar.
(ii) It empowers citizens to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
(iii) The SC can issue writs including Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto.
(iv) This right can never be suspended, even during a national emergency.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Called 'heart and soul' by Ambedkar (i correct). Allows moving SC (ii correct). SC issues 5 types of writs (iii correct). (iv) is wrong because Art. 32 CAN be suspended during a National Emergency under Art. 359. Option 2 includes (iv). Option 3 excludes (iii). Option 4 includes (iv).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Sagarmala Programme' aims to:
options: Promote port-led development and coastal economic growth
questions.correctAnswer: Promote port-led development and coastal economic growth
questions.explanation: Sagarmala focuses on port modernization, connectivity, port-led industrialization, and coastal community development. 'Clean beaches' is wrong — too narrow. 'Deep-sea fishing' is wrong — that's Blue Revolution. 'Underwater tunnels' is wrong — not Sagarmala's scope.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Vernacular Press Act' of 1878 was enacted during the viceroyalty of:
questions.explanation: Lord Lytton (Viceroy 1876-80) enacted the Vernacular Press Act to control Indian language newspapers. 'Lord Ripon' is wrong — he repealed this Act in 1882. 'Lord Dufferin' is wrong — Viceroy 1884-88. 'Lord Curzon' is wrong — Viceroy 1899-1905.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Digital India' programme was launched in which year?
questions.explanation: Digital India was launched on 1 July 2015 to transform India into a digitally empowered society. '2014' is wrong — Make in India was that year. '2016' is wrong — too late. '2017' is wrong — far too late.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Inter-State River Water Disputes are adjudicated by tribunals, not the Supreme Court.
Reason (R): Article 262 empowers Parliament to provide for adjudication of inter-state river disputes and can exclude the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in such matters.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Inter-state water disputes go to tribunals (A correct). Article 262 provides this mechanism and can exclude SC jurisdiction (R correct and is the constitutional basis for A). Option 2 is wrong because R is the exact constitutional provision enabling A. Option 3 is wrong because R is correct. Option 4 is wrong because A is correct.
